_about: Real malicious package@version pairs from documented supply-chain incidents. Used by `cargo test --test corpus` to verify that npmguard's risk engine surfaces signals on packages we know to be compromised. References are public post-incident write-ups; the packages themselves should NEVER be installed.

entries.name: lodahs
entries.incident: Typosquat of lodash, flagged MAL-2025-25502 by OSV malware namespace

_notes: Most malicious versions from Shai-Hulud are now unpublished from npm; the registry returns 'version not found in packument' and the test treats that as a successful detection (unpublishing is itself a confirmed-bad signal). Live entries like `lodahs@0.0.1-security` are kept because npm's security team replaces compromised packages with stub versions retaining the MAL-* OSV advisory — these stay queryable and are the most useful live signal to test against. This corpus will grow as we curate more such entries; the design doc earlier referenced `axios@1.12.0` as a Mar 2026 compromise, but the actually-malicious version was unpublished — 1.12.0 only carries a routine SSRF advisory, so it was removed from this list to avoid implying it's malware.
